newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines begins witch-hunt for peso speculators.
newsitem.headline: Philippines begins witch-hunt for peso speculators.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Monday it was looking into last week's heavy speculation which led to the de facto peso devaluation and will punish any banks which broke its rules.
Governor Gabriel Singson told reporters that the Bank was checking into who had oversold and overbought positions since last Wednesday.
On Friday the Central Bank succumbed to repeated speculative attacks on the currency, allowing the peso to plunge 11.5 percent.
"We'll have to impose sanctions on these banks (that exceeded their limits). We're calling up the banks, those who bought heavily and trying to find out what haplpened," Singson said.
The Central Bank limits the amount of long or short dollar position onshore banks may hold and makes it difficult to buy large amounts of dollars without underlying business justification.
It is also looking into the non-deliverable forward market in the peso, which mostly operates in Singapore.
Some estimates have put the amount of outstanding peso/dollar contracts in the market at up to $5 billion. The average daily volume in the onshore peso market is less than $1 billion.
"We will review that market because we're finding out they could be using it for speculation," Singson said.
Currently eight onshore foreign and local banks have derivatives licenses.
The review will be finished in a week's time, he said.
